title: US military boards, searches and sinks vessel allegedly supporting Los Choneros narco-terrorists
text:
Video captures USS San Antonio Marines boarding and sinking a Los Choneros narco-terrorist floating refueling station in the Eastern Pacific.

SOUTHCOM said the operation targeted a vessel tied to Los Choneros, which it described as a violent narco-terrorist organization.
"On Sept. 2, at the direction of #SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan, and in coordination and collaboration with the Government of Ecuador, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere successfully interdicted a vessel operating as a floating refueling station in support of illicit at-sea drug trafficking operations in international waters of the Eastern Pacific," SOUTHCOM said in a statement. U.S. Marines The military said multiple individuals were removed from the vessel and transferred to Ecuadorian authorities.
In its statement, SOUTHCOM said the operation"cuts off a critical node" in the alleged drug traffickers' illicit activities. It did not disclose the specific location of the operation. The action was taken in support of the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition and JTF-WHEM's mission to dismantle narco-terrorist networks in the region, according to SOUTHCOM.
US MILITARY LAUNCHES FIRST AUTONOMOUS WARFARE COMMAND TO DEPLOY UNMANNED SYSTEMS ACROSS LATIN AMERICA U.S. military forces intercepted a vessel in the Eastern Pacific that SOUTHCOM said was operating as a floating refueling station in support of illicit drug trafficking.
"We are taking decisive action to dismantle and destroy sophisticated logistics networks used by narco-terrorists to traffic drugs and spread violence throughout the Western Hemisphere," Donovan said. "This operation demonstrated the elite capabilities and precision of Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere, which is on watch in the region to apply total systemic friction on these networks," he added. Video of the operation released by SOUTHCOM shows military personnel intercepting the vessel before boarding it and ultimately sinking the craft.
U.S. Marines and sailors from the USS San Antonio boarded and searched a vessel allegedly supporting the Los Choneros narco-terrorist organization, according to SOUTHCOM.
"The message is clear: the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition will continue to apply total systemic friction on narco-terrorists," SOUTHCOM wrote. Following that strike, the Trump administration's campaign targeting suspected cartel vessels has resulted in at least 227 deaths across 68 reported strikes over roughly one year. Fox News Digital's Eric Mack contributed to this report.
